description: Examination records with no ID are excluded, so only real patient IDs form groups.

c.request: Count the Examination records for each `ID` and express each count as a share of the total. For the IDs whose share is above the average share, what are their average record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share beats the average share? Give one unrounded row. Examination records with no ID are excluded, so only real patient IDs form groups.
c.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), s AS (SELECT ID, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

b.request: Counting only Examination records with a non-null `ID`, grouped by `ID`, compute each patient's record count and its share of the total count of those non-null-ID records. Then, for the IDs whose share exceeds the average share across IDs, return one unrounded row with their average record count, their average share, and the average of (share minus the overall average share)
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), s AS (SELECT ID, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_diff FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

a.request: Group the Examination records by `ID` and count the records in each group. Records whose `ID` is missing are dropped first and count nowhere. Divide each group's count by the total of all group counts to get its share, find the plain average of the shares, and keep the groups whose share is above it. Return one unrounded row with: the kept groups' average record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), s AS (SELECT ID, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s), k AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share, a.avg_share FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM k

d.request: Count the Examination records for each `ID`, excluding records that have no ID so that only real patient IDs form groups, and express each count as a share of the total. For the IDs whose share is above the average share, what are their average record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share beats the average share? Give one unrounded row.
d.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), s AS (SELECT ID, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
